text:
incident-bot: PAGER: latency-surge detected on serving-region-us-west-2. p95 and p99 for streaming endpoints (kv/stream) spiked >3x over the last 5m. Paging oncall-miguel (priority: P1). :rotating_light:
oncall-miguel: got it. I'm looking at dashboards now. Initial thought: anomalous tail from a subset of GPU nodes, QPS steady.
dana: seeing errors in node metrics: repeated ECC correctable events on node gpu-34*. Also temp on that rack elevated.
sara: client reports streaming stalls for long-running streams (>= 8k tokens). p50 ok, p95/p99 bad. Some sessions saw stall ~10-20s.
lee: checking routing logs — a small subset of requests were routed to a legacy quantized variant on the same node pool. Possibly KV cache miss + kernel fallback causing stalls.
infra-jen: can we pin which physical host? I'm seeing device ids: gpu-34a/gpu-34b with repeated "correctable ECC" counts and device_util oscillation.
oncall-miguel: infra-jen can you quarantine gpu-34a/34b from the pool (live drain) and re-route traffic? We need quick mitigation.
infra-jen: initiating drain: 
```bash
# cordon and migrate
redwoodctl nodes drain gpu-34a --reason "ECC-correctable-spike" --live
redwoodctl nodes drain gpu-34b --reason "ECC-correctable-spike" --live
```
infra-jen: also adding +2 hot-standby capacity in the region to absorb stateful KV-heavy sessions.
ali: pushed routing rule to prioritize "stable-variant-v2" for streaming calls for the next 30m. Fallback still allowed but with stricter health checks.
eng-runtime: quick note — the quantized legacy path has a known pathologic interaction when ECC corrections trigger retries in the kernel; we've seen tail amplification. Recommend disabling that variant if drain doesn't stabilize.
customer-ops: which customers are impacted? I see elevated error counts for a handful of enterprise tenants on us-west-2, mostly long-chat workloads. We should notify affected customers if we expect >30m mitigation.
oncall-miguel: doing customer impact triage now. sara, can you pull example trace for one impacted session? Need request ids.
sara: grabbing a trace: request_id=rt-0a1b2c3d stream session 9876. Stack shows stall when kernel fallback attempts to recompile kv cache and waits on device memory. Extract: 
```
Trace rt-0a1b2c3d:
  step: token_emit (t=0s -> ok)
  step: kv_fetch (t=2.1s -> retry)
  step: kernel_fallback (t=12.8s -> stalled, waiting on device)
  step: stream_timeout_retry (t=22.9s)
```
sara: so it's reproducible on these device ids.
eng-runtime: patch idea: short-circuit fallback for streaming sessions to avoid long recompiles. But that's a code change; we can do config-level skip for fallback on the variant.
oncall-miguel: for immediate live mitigation: 1) drain the two nodes (infra-jen started) 2) increase capacity (infra-jen started) 3) blacklist legacy quant variant for streaming (ali done) 4) enable aggressive KV cache warmup for new sessions (eng-runtime can toggle)
eng-runtime: toggled KV warmup for new streaming sessions to aggressive mode. Also temporarily disabled kernel fallback for streaming on legacy path by config flag.
ops-bot: Deploy log: routing-change v2026.03.15-801 applied by ali at 1882223450.
infra-jen: drain completed. Nodes cordoned and live sessions migrated. Observability: p95 dropped ~40% in last 3m, p99 improving but still ~1.8x baseline.
dana: GPU ECC correctable counters are still incrementing on gpu-34c (same rack). Thermal sensors show ambient increase ~8C over baseline. Fans spiking.
lee: starting probe to isolate cooling issue with host-level vendor tools; may request manual rack cooling or switchover.
oncall-miguel: do we need to evacuate rack and schedule maintenance? If hardware noisy, prefer quarantine and replace next maintenance window. For customers, set expectation: mitigation in progress, next update in 30m.
customer-ops: drafting customer message: "We detected intermittent streaming stalls affecting long-running sessions in US-West. We've applied routing mitigations and removed affected nodes; engineers continue to monitor. We expect restoration within 30-60 minutes. If you see persistent stalls, please reply with request ids." Shall I send?
oncall-miguel: yes, send now. Mark impacted tenants and include PSA.
ali: sent customer-notice to subset list at 1882223610.
eng-runtime: still seeing a handful of retries surfaced in traces but no new long stalls after drifts and route changes. Kernel logs show ECC corrections triggered device de-scheduling briefly: 
```
[device gpu-34a] ECC_CORRECTABLE=++  delta=27 within 5m
[driver] kernel_fallback: sched_wait=12000ms -> aborted
```
eng-runtime: we'll follow up with longer-term fix: avoid expensive fallback during streaming; also improve health check sensitivity for ECC counters.
danA: (typo fix) dana: after evacuation, thermal trending still high — vendor cooling ticket opened (ticket# VC-5543). They recommend inspecting airflow in rack and potential fan replacement.
noncall-miguel: next steps summary: 
- monitor p99 for next 60m (oncall)
- hardware quarantine for affected hosts (infra)
- follow-up engineering patch to skip fallback on streaming (eng-runtime backlog)
- customer communications and post-incident note (customer-ops/product)
any objections?
eng-runtime: ack, will open a short RFC for rollback-safe skip of fallback and add unit tests.
infra-jen: scheduling maintenance window for 6h from now for physical inspection; will coordinate with hardware vendor.
customer-ops: update sent. No major escalations yet.
oncall-miguel: thanks all — continue monitoring. I'll update this thread in 30m or on any customer-impact change. :thumbsup:
